ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and intended payment processors (including UberEats and DoorDash payout entities) against: (i) the Gibraltar sanctions list administered by the Gibraltar Sanctions Unit; (ii) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list; (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (v) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; and (vi) the GFSC adverse media and World-Check style PEP databases. Positive PEP matches require enhanced due diligence (EDD), senior management approval, and source-of-wealth documentation per GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes Part B. Sanctions hits require immediate reporting to the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit (GFIU) and transaction blocking; formation must cease pending OFAC/Gibraltar authorization. Ongoing monitoring is mandatory for the life of the ELP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House e-Registry (Registrar of Companies of Gibraltar online portal, operated under the Companies Act 2014 and the Limited Partnerships Act 1995)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that the name be expressed entirely in Latin characters using the English alphabet; no non-Latin or transliterated scripts are permitted in the registered name; names must be in English or a Latin-script European language; the suffix 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'LP' must appear at the end of the name unless an exemption is granted; the name must not be misleading as to the nature, object, or scale of the partnership's business; ghost kitchen and virtual brand activity must be reflected accurately in the name and statement of objects to avoid a mis-description rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written representation to the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of the rejection notice under Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) s. 29; the representation must demonstrate that the proposed name is not misleading, does not infringe existing registered names or trademarks, and does not fall within prohibited categories; if the Registrar confirms refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar by filing a Form 6A originating motion within 42 days of the refusal; alternatively, the applicant may reserve an alternative name via the e-Registry portal and resubmit; extension of the 30-day reservation window may be requested with payment of the prescribed extension fee where evidence of genuine administrative delay in KYC completion is provided.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted — a physical registered office within Gibraltar is mandatory under the Limited Partnerships Act 1995, and a standalone virtual office address cannot satisfy the statutory requirement; however, a licensed registered agent may provide a serviced physical registered office address where all statutory mail is physically and digitally forwarded to the general partner, provided that the agent retains physical possession of the registered office premises and satisfies GFSC substance and compliance supervision requirements; full virtual operation (no physical Gibraltar presence) is permissible for the underlying ghost kitchen delivery business only where the ELP operates through sub-contracted local dark kitchen operators abroad, but the ELP itself must retain the registered office and a licensed general partner in Gibraltar; the GFSC expects the ELP to demonstrate commercial substance through board/partner decision-making records, retained books and records in Gibraltar, and a Gibraltar-resident agent exercising supervisory control.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10 percent — a quantified low-to-moderate risk that the GFSC or the Registrar of Companies will conduct an unannounced physical on-site inspection of the registered office within the first operating year, driven primarily by the low-risk standard AML classification of delivery-only cloud kitchen operations, the presence of a licensed registered agent, and the absence of a physical operational footprint in Gibraltar; inspection risk rises to approximately 18 percent if the ELP is reclassified as higher risk due to high-volume third-party payouts through UberEats and DoorDash, or if sanctions screening flags any new partner jurisdiction.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Gibraltar) — registration, exempted-status and annual-return provisions; Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) — corporate general partner incorporation and registered-office duties; Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), s. 18 — exemption certificate for non-resident-controlled entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies — Companies House, HM Government of Gibraltar, 18 Cooperage Lane, Gibraltar GX11 1AA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 — Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership with Exempted Status endorsement, together with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, filed under the Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act 2019.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an exempted limited partnership; each limited partner's contribution is contractually fixed in the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be paid in cash or in kind. No escrow account is legally required for an unregulated ELP; for AML-consistent banking practice the initial contributions should be settled into the partnership's operating account at a Gibraltar-licensed bank, with source-of-funds evidence, within 15 business days of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That this Company, as corporate General Partner, subscribes for its general partner interest in KITCHEN EXCELLENCE ELP and ratifies the execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and the limited partners' subscription statements; (2) That the registered office of the Partnership in Gibraltar is adopted as the Company's registered premises at 18 Cooperage Lane; (3) That the Designated Representative is appointed Managing Officer to file all statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies; (4) That officers are authorized to implement formation, food licensing, environmental, fire-safety, banking and payment-rails matters; (5) That application for exempt status be submitted to the Commissioner of Income Tax and any director is authorized to sign.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation of the Corporate General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies — Companies House, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the proposed corporate general partner (private company limited by shares, exempt-company eligible); execute the statutory declaration of compliance; file the incorporation application with Companies House; pay the registration fee; obtain the Certificate of Incorporation. The registered office must be a physical address in Gibraltar (18 Cooperage Lane, through the registered agent).
required_dossiers: Notarized passport copies of each subscriber director and shareholder
Memorandum and Articles of Association (two certified copies)
Signed statutory declaration of compliance (Company Act form CO1)
Registered-office consent letter from the Gibraltar registered agent
Address verification and bank reference for each officer (AML2013 due diligence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file an amended declaration of compliance within 14 days under the Companies Act 2014; registry-error corrections are free of charge, otherwise a reduced re-filing fee applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar; official Government portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi. Import duties and excise matters are administered by the Customs and Excise Department, HM Customs Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership must: (1) instruct a licensed Gibraltar corporate service provider and maintain a registered office in Gibraltar; (2) file the partnership registration application under the Gibraltar Limited Partnerships legislation with the Registrar of Companies and obtain a Gibraltar partnership registration number; (3) register the partnership for tax at the Income Tax Office by submitting the prescribed partnership registration particulars, thereby obtaining a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number; (4) identify each general and limited partner, supplying the partner's foreign TIN or an explanation where no TIN is held; and (5) if importing or holding duty-suspended or excise goods, register separately with the Customs and Excise Department. There is no separate Gibraltar VAT registration or VAT ID because Gibraltar does not operate a VAT/GST system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. The Exempted Limited Partnership is tax-transparent by default under Gibraltar income tax legislation; each partner is separately chargeable on their distributive share of partnership profits. Statutory and administrative elections are limited to the tax treatment of non-resident partners' Gibraltar-source income, the allocation of profits under the partnership agreement, and anti-hybrid/compliance elections required to respect OECD BEPS Action 2 and prevent double non-taxation. The partnership cannot elect to be taxed as an entity-level company without changing its legal form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST purposes; there is no turnover-based indirect-tax registration threshold in Gibraltar. Registration obligations arise under customs/excise law for businesses importing or holding excisable goods, and not from ordinary ghost-kitchen or food-delivery revenues. If the Gibraltar entity separately carries on a UK taxable business, UK VAT registration may be required at the standard GBP 85,000 turnover threshold or sooner for non-established businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar does not impose a mandatory electronic-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API connectivity, or digital stamping regime for domestic supplies. Ordinary delivery and food-service invoices may be issued without fiscal authorisation. Customs import/export declarations must be filed electronically with HM Customs Gibraltar, and platform settlement data from UberEats, DoorDash or similar operators should be retained as contemporaneous books-and-records evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in Gibraltar because there is no VAT/GST regime and therefore no statutory zero-rating claim exists for goods or services. Goods physically exported from Gibraltar are outside the domestic excise duty base only when the applicable customs export procedure is completed. Offshore services supplied to non-resident recipients are not subject to Gibraltar consumption tax. If the entity is separately registered for UK VAT through a UK fixed establishment, UK export zero-rating rules may apply to qualifying goods and services under UK legislation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Because Gibraltar has no VAT/GST, there is no VAT export-clawback mechanism; however, false or incomplete customs declarations can result in recovery of unpaid duty, penalties of up to 100% of the duty value, forfeiture of goods, and criminal prosecution. Fraudulent misdescription of export transactions may also reopen Gibraltar income tax assessments beyond the normal six-year window, with unlimited time limits in cases of deliberate non-disclosure. Intercompany payments connected with export or platform revenues should be supported by contemporaneous contracts, transfer-pricing documentation, and foreign currency repatriation evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of England (monetary anchor for sterling and ultimate lender-of-last-resort for the Gibraltar pound) and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) (prudential and AML/CTF supervisor of all banks and payment institutions in Gibraltar). Gibraltar has no separate Central Bank or Foreign Exchange Administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar issues its own currency, the Gibraltar pound (GIP), legally pegged 1:1 to the British pound sterling (GBP), with GIP and GBP banknotes circulating interchangeably. Both current-account flows (trade settlements, delivery-platform payouts, royalties, management fees) and capital-account flows (partner capital contributions, profit distributions, redemption/repurchase of partnership interests) are fully convertible without prior authorisation, retention limits, or central bank approval. Profit remittance is unrestricted; only standard FATCA/CRS reporting, GFSC transaction monitoring, and sanctions screening duties apply. Non-resident partners may hold, settle, and remit in GBP, EUR, or USD without any mandatory conversion ratio or balance-sheet conversion mandate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Gibraltar and the United Kingdom impose no statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export or operating receipts. All delivery-platform settlements (UberEats, DoorDash) may be retained in the receipt currency; any voluntary conversion to GBP/EUR is governed solely by commercial treasury policy and documented in the partnership's cash-management and risk framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Investment Sweep Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. GFSC-authorised Electronic Money Institutions and UK-FCA-authorised EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, specialised fintech cash managers) are viable as clearing-only sub-ledgers for rapid cross-border settlement of ghost-kitchen payouts, but they cannot serve as the primary regulated custody rail for the Capital Escrow Account because they are not licensed deposit-takers. Legal constraints: EMI funds must be safeguarded under e-money regulations and are not protected by the Gibraltar Deposit Guarantee Scheme; EMI accounts require an upstream top-up and downstream sweep from a Tier 1 licensed bank; and GFSC AML/CTF rules require a regulated local introducing agent to complete the beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds dossier. Feasibility rating: Medium - high utility for operational float, low utility for statutory capital escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted; no statutory requirement exists for directors or non-resident partners of a Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership to appear physically before the bank. However, in practice Tier 1 banks require a live biometric video interview with a certified AML officer, a notarised partnership deed, and the participation of the statutory registered agent in Gibraltar to verify partner identities and projected delivery-platform revenue streams. A fully unrestricted online account opening without human verification is generally not available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident pass-through ELP with no minimum capital requirement and a flexible partner register raises beneficial-ownership ambiguity and potential anonymous-vehicle concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Limited Partnership Deed; GFSC beneficial-ownership register filing identifying every individual partner or controller holding 25% or more; certified passports of all partners; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, tax returns, exit-event liquidity records); formation-agent structural diagram and chain-of-title memo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Delivery-platform settlement volume concentrated in UberEats/DoorDash without a written operating contract is treated as a third-party payment red flag and potential money-laundering-through-goods typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counter-signed merchant/operator agreements with each delivery platform; monthly payout and settlement statements reconciled to the general ledger; ghost-kitchen sublicence or facility-use agreements; updated food business registration and kitchen operating permits; revenue-recognition memorandum from the independent accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections routed from offshore jurisdictions (e.g., Cayman feeder vehicles) trigger enhanced due diligence on the origin of capital and tax-transparency scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licence confirmation and FATCA/CRS registration certificates of the remitting bank; audited financial statements of the contributing partner; ultimate-beneficial-owner structure chart; tax-transparency opinion confirming the ELP is not used for hybrid-mismatch avoidance; board resolution or partnership resolution authorising the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed use of fintech EMI wallets or virtual-brand cash-management tokens raises concerns of unreported payment channels, commingling, or sanctions-circumvention.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written contracts with each EMI/platform wallet provider; clear diagram of the clearing path from EMI to the Tier 1 operational account; ledger policy prohibiting commingling of partner and operating funds; completed sanctions screening (HMT, OFAC, EU Consolidated List) with negative hits; quarterly AML/CTF compliance attestation by the Gibraltar appointed officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All partner capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 to the Tier 1 Capital Escrow Account or Operational Account, with Field 70 narrative: 'Capital Contribution to Gibraltar ELP - [Partnership Legal Name]', and, where supported by the correspondent bank, ISO 20022 payment purpose code CAPC (capital payment) or INTC (intra-company transfer) as a fallback. The receiving bank will verify remitter FATCA/CRS status, screen the UBO list against sanctions, and require the partnership's registered agent to confirm the commercial substance of the ghost-kitchen operation before funds are released from escrow. Any injection channelled through an unregulated fintech wallet, crypto-asset, or non-GFSC/non-FCA intermediary must be rechannelled through the regulated escrow path prior to operational deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier invoices and international food-service/equipment settlements; (2) UK Faster Payments and CHAPS for same-day GBP-denominated domestic disbursements; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EUR-denominated supply payments; (4) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600, issued via the Tier 1 bank, for high-value vendor, fit-out, or franchise arrangements requiring documentary security; (5) direct integration of UberEats/DoorDash payout flows into a segregated settlement ledger designated as a non-deposit-taking clearing rail. Every MT103 must include the beneficiary's full legal name, IBAN or account number, purpose code/narrative, and must be pre-validated against GFSC sanctions and denied-party screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (GBP/EUR, GBP/USD) with a GFSC-licensed credit institution or FCA-authorised broker, tenors up to 12 months, collateralised by contracted operating cash flow.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible strictly for hedging non-deliverable-currency exposures arising from cross-border supply contracts where no underlying deliverable market exists; requires board-approved hedge mandate and counterparty credit limits.

Cross-currency swaps (currency interest-rate swaps) permissible for long-dated partner-capital or acquisition exposures, including GBP/EUR floating-to-floating and fixed-to-floating structures, executed only under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a GFSC-licensed bank.

FX spot contracts and short-term FX swaps for operational cash sweeps between GIP/GBP, EUR, and USD; no exchange-control authorisation, surrender obligation, or central bank notification is triggered by any of the above instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ELP Annual Return (Companies House Form AR-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each annual anniversary of the ELP's establishment date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 100 (approx USD 130) plus daily escalation up to GBP 500; continued non-compliance for 6 months may trigger compulsory strike-off of the ELP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the ELP establishment anniversary, with mandatory interim filing within 21 days of any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty up to GBP 5,000 (approx USD 6,500) plus potential restricted registration or criminal prosecution for deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ELP Tax Transparency Annual Status Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (through the ELP's appointed tax agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December following the end of each tax year, or as specified in the Income Tax Act notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on any attributable tax at statutory rate (currently 1% per month); repeated violations may result in the loss of pass-through treatment for the ELP or the disqualification of the tax agent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for an ELP unless (i) the partnership exceeds Gibraltar Companies Act audit exemption thresholds (annual turnover above GBP 10.2m, balance sheet above GBP 5.1m, or more than 50 employees), (ii) the partnership agreement or a majority of partners elects an audit, or (iii) a lender or other material counterparty contractually requires a certified audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Gibraltar (Companies Act 2014 and Companies (Accounts) Regulations) for statutory financial statements; ELPs may apply FRS 101/102 equivalent for small entity treatment where eligible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The ELP must maintain a beneficial ownership register (as required under the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Act 2017) identifying all individuals holding more than 25% interest, voting rights, or control. An annual confirmation must be submitted electronically through the BOSS system on each establishment anniversary; any shareholding or interest transfer during the year must be reflected and refreshed in the register within 21 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 4,000 (only if triggered; otherwise no mandatory cost)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (applied to chargeable corporate partners and permanent establishments; the Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and not itself a taxable entity)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific corporate tax holidays or preferential headline rates; the effective benefit arises from strict territoriality: income that neither arises in nor is derived from Gibraltar is excluded from charge unless attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment. Streamed delivery-platform revenues are chargeable only to the extent the underlying ghost-kitchen operation is carried on in Gibraltar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Designated Gibraltar Corporate Gross Income Tax Return — Form GIT-C1; filed through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-Returns portal at https://www.ito.gov.gi/e-returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly payments on account may be required when the assessed gross income exceeds the amount for which automatic assessment applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The completed return is due no later than 30 November immediately following the end of the chargeable accounting period (e.g., accounting period ended 31 December 2024 is due by 30 November 2025), unless an extended notice is served by the Commissioner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable accounting period start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the partnership fiscal year; for an ELP with non-resident limited partners, enter the actual ELP period-end and attach the partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income arising in or derived from Gibraltar, including commissions, delivery-platform settlements and virtual-brand licence fees received through the Gibson kitchen operation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Gibraltar-source trading receipts. Separate UberEats, DoorDash and other payout aggregator receipts by bank country; exclude foreign-source income but disclose it in the supplementary schedule to evidence territoriality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable trading expenses: food procurement, rent, utilities, equipment leases, delivery-partner settlement costs, staff wages, insurance and platform commission
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are restricted to expenses incurred wholly and exclusively for the Gibraltar trade. Related-party mark-ups on procurement or delivery services must satisfy the arm’s length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted chargeable gross income before statutory deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ELP is transparent and the limited partner has no Gibraltar permanent establishment, insert zero or proportionally nil income and attach a partner residency certificate.
Available to the partner or Gibraltar permanent establishment only; limited loss relief cannot be passed through tax-transparent partners without a valid partnership allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, payments on account and DTA credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits under the Gibraltar-United Kingdom double taxation arrangement by attaching Form GTR-3 tax residence certificate and withholding certificates from the source tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs an automatic fixed penalty of GBP 100; if the return remains outstanding more than 6 months, a further 5% of the tax shown is added. Interest accrues daily at the statutory base rate plus 2%. A daily late-filing surcharge of GBP 25, capped at GBP 1,000, is levied for each day the return is outstanding after the due date. Deliberate non-filing raises penalties up to 200% of the tax due and may trigger criminal assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar does not impose statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a Gibraltar entity, including an ELP, to its partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar has a limited double taxation arrangement, most notably with the United Kingdom. To invoke treaty relief: (1) apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a tax residence certificate (Form GTR-3) for the general partner or the corporate partner claiming residence; (2) request a UK residence certificate from HM Revenue & Customs where the partner is UK-resident; (3) submit both certificates to the source payer before the distribution; (4) for UK-source payments, file a formal claim under the UK-Gibraltar arrangement within three years of the payment if withholding has been applied; (5) treat the arrangement as excluding Gibraltar-source dividends from UK income and vice versa. For jurisdictions with TIEAs but no comprehensive DTA, no zero-rate is automatically available; the Tax Information Exchange Agreement is used only for exchange of information and recovery assistance, not for withholding relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 0% withholding tax on royalty payments and 0% withholding tax on interest paid by Gibraltar-resident persons. Treaty rates: 0% under the UK-Gibraltar arrangement for eligible royalties and interest; beneficial ownership and economic substance must be demonstrated, otherwise anti-abuse rules may reclassify hybrid payments as distributions or service fees.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GBP 10,000,000 — mandatory Local File is triggered where annual gross turnover of the Gibraltar taxpayer exceeds GBP 10,000,000; a Master File is required when the multinational group’s consolidated annual revenue exceeds GBP 50,000,000, and Country-by-Country notification is due when the group exceeds GBP 750,000,000 in consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. The Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations 2019 require resident companies and partnerships engaging in relevant activities to maintain core income-generating activities, premises, employees, board meetings and operating expenditure in Gibraltar. A virtual-brand ghost-kitchen model falls within the ‘distribution and service centre’ relevant activity where order aggregation, delivery logistics, brand management and customer settlement occur in Gibraltar. The ELP must document staffing, premises, service contracts and decision-making; failure renders the arrangement a shell company and triggers denial of tax residence benefits, recharacterisation and civil sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting UberEats, DoorDash or other food-delivery platform settlement amounts; underreporting virtual-brand turnover; manufacturing artificial partnership losses through inflated related-party food-delivery charges; filing a nil return while operating a commercially active ghost-kitchen facility in Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil tax-geared penalty of 100% to 200% of the additional tax due; statutory interest at base rate plus 2% per annum; late-filing surcharges up to GBP 1,000; criminal prosecution under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act carrying an unlimited fine and imprisonment for up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and every person concerned in the management of the ELP may be assessed personally where the partnership is treated as an artificial arrangement. Courts may pierce the partnership veil, impose joint and several restitution orders, issue travel bans for tax absconders, and disqualify individuals from acting as directors or general partners for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the ELP registration and Gibraltar bank account purely as a routing vehicle for UK and EU ghost-kitchen revenues; having no premises, no local employees, no board meetings in Gibraltar, and no decision-making relating to brand procurement, delivery logistics or invoicing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may deny the territoriality benefit by asserting a Gibraltar permanent establishment or chargeable presence, recharacterise circular payments, impose fines under the Economic Substance Regulations of up to GBP 500,000, and strike the partnership from the Gibraltar Register. Professional enablers may be fined under the general anti-abuse framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and limited partners participating in management face personal liability for unpaid tax and penalties. Directors or managers may be subject to disqualification, civil recovery of assets exported from Gibraltar, and travel restrictions where unpaid tax exceeds statutory thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payouts from virtual-brand owners into the ELP bank account; commingling delivery-platform settlements with partner capital without legitimate commercial documentation; executing rapid onward transfers to non-resident partners or suppliers in connection with ghost kitchens that have no physical trace; failing to conduct customer due diligence on platform settlement arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the Gibraltar Criminal Justice (Money Laundering) Act and the Proceeds of Crime Act exposes the ELP to fines up to GBP 1,000,000, asset forfeiture, confiscation of platform balances, and suspension or revocation of the statutory ghost-kitchen operating licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual officers or general partners may be imprisoned for up to 14 years for money laundering offences; directors may be ordered to pay compensation for funds lost to suspicious transactions; travel bans and international asset-freezing orders may be imposed pending criminal investigation or extradition proceedings.
